q1: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2: WITH SOLD_TO_RED AS ( SELECT DISTINCT O.SALES_ID FROM ORDERS AS O INNER JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' ) SELECT DISTINCT SP.NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS SP WHERE NOT EXISTS( SELECT 1 FROM SOLD_TO_RED WHERE SP.SALES_ID = SOLD_TO_RED.SALES_ID )

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 uses a subquery with COUNT(*) to check if there are no orders for the 'RED' company, while Q2 uses a CTE (Common Table Expression) with a NOT EXISTS clause to achieve the same goal. The difference lies in how they handle the subquery results. Q1 will return salespersons who have no orders for the 'RED' company, even if they have orders for other companies. Q2, on the other hand, will return salespersons who have no orders for the 'RED' company and no orders for any other company.
